The TACT1 program was developed at the NASA Lewis Research Center.
The program consists of approximately 6200 lines of FORTRAN IV code and requires about 60,000 words of storage.
The program can handle a turbine blade or vane equipped with a central coolant-plenum insert from which coolant air flows through holes to impinge on the inner surface of the blade shell.
The spent impingement air is assumed to flow chordwise and be discharged through a split or drilled trailing edge and through film-cooling holes.
The program does not allow for radial flow of the spent impingement air.
The program uses finite-difference equations to model the transient energy and momentum balances in the blade and coolant channels.
The program includes built-in heat-transfer correlations for impingement cooling, forced-convection channel flow, and forced convection over pin fins.
The program can handle a blade with a ceramic thermal-barrier coating over a metallic substrate.
The program can adjust either the coolant-supply pressure or the coolant-inlet flow rate in the outermost iteration loop to achieve an overall coolant mass balance.
The program can produce plots of temperature and pressure distributions along the blade surface using a TSS/360 graphics package.
The program can handle time-dependent hot-gas boundary conditions, with multiple sets of boundary condition data specified at different times.
The program can handle mixed radial-axial flow of the hot gas stream, allowing the chordwise cutting planes to be at non-constant radii.
The program can handle a limited capability for film cooling, with the user specifying either the wall heat-transfer coefficient or an effectiveness correlation.
The program uses a specific correlation for impingement into a concave surface at the leading-edge stagnation point.
The program includes a table of air properties as a function of temperature at 20 atmospheres pressure.
